First public release of **trackparse**, a parser that turns music track strings into structured metadata. The spec behind it is shared by every port.

```js
import { parse } from "trackparse";

parse("01. Wilkinson ft. Becky Hill - Afterglow (Sub Focus VIP Remix) [Official Video]");
// artists:  Wilkinson (primary), Becky Hill (featured, "ft.")
// title:    "Afterglow"
// versions: remix by Sub Focus, modifiers ["vip"]
// junk:     "Official Video" (video) · position: 1
```

### Highlights

- **Extract, don't delete.** Featured artists, remixers, producers, version type (remix, VIP, bootleg, extended, radio, original, live, remaster with year, sped up…), explicit/clean flags, track numbers, timestamps and junk ("Official Video", "4K", "Free Download") each come back as their own field, next to a clean title.
- **Artists as a list.** Splits on `&` `,` `x` `vs` `/` `+` `with` `and`, uses the leftmost feat marker, keeps the joiners so `format()` can rebuild the string, and never splits `AC/DC`, `2 Unlimited` or `Blink-182`. Names that must never be split go in `knownArtists`.
- **Modes** for store titles, YouTube titles (pipes, ` by `, quoted titles, uploader fallback) and filenames.
- **Unicode-aware.** NFC, every dash and bracket variant, Cyrillic, CJK and diacritics, with diacritic-insensitive dedup.
- **Zero dependencies.** ESM + CJS + TypeScript types, Node ≥ 18. `parse` never throws.

### Spec 0.1.0

- `spec/SPEC.md`: rules R0–R12 written to be portable (hand-written scanners, no regex lookaround), so the JS, Python and Rust ports can give byte-identical output.
- **11,889 shared fixtures**: 898 handwritten (including regressions from real-world parsers) and 10,991 from a combinatorial generator whose expected values are built from ground-truth atoms, not from the parser.
- The JS reference implementation passes all of them with an empty skip list.

Python (PyPI) and Rust (crates.io) ports are planned against the same fixtures.
